design: Post-hoc evaluation of all 96 immutable snapshots; no new model calls. Exploratory, not a preregistered model ranking.
category_na_policy: A category absent by task design is omitted and weights are renormalized. A failed or timed-out applicable evaluation is not N/A and blocks a complete composite.
overall_policy: No overall score until every component is present and valid. Automated evidence score uses 30:35:20 normalized to 100, only with all three components present; it is not an overall code-quality grade.
own_test_policy: Only candidate-added tests, not supplied public tests. Same 4/5/5/6 seeded reference defects per task. A kill requires a test passing on the positive reference to fail on that mutant. Skips/import errors/timeouts are disclosed. Reference portability failures make the mutation score unavailable. No added tests gives 0, without changing original correctness.

performance.memory: separate tracemalloc run; Python allocations only
performance.note: Execution performance, not model time. Sequential, same pinned Python and machine; per-task values only, with no fixed speed bonus.

manual_review.required_evidence: Reviewer, source path and line, explanation; blinded model labels where possible.

anchors.0: Cannot follow core logic; misleading names obscure behavior.
anchors.1: Core behavior requires substantial reconstruction; several confusing constructs.
anchors.2: Logic is understandable, but naming or control flow repeatedly slows review.
anchors.3: Clear names and flow; non-obvious invariants explained; minor friction.
anchors.4: Core invariants, state transitions and edge cases are easy to trace without redundant explanation.

anchors.0: Core responsibilities are inseparable or global shared state breaks isolation.
anchors.1: Repeated business logic or strong coupling makes a simple change risky.
anchors.2: Reasonable boundaries with notable duplication/coupling or needless abstractions.
anchors.3: Responsibilities and state ownership are clear; limited avoidable duplication.
anchors.4: Small cohesive components and explicit interfaces support a concrete likely change; no needless machinery.

anchors.0: Errors/data integrity cannot be reasoned about; resources leak on common paths.
anchors.1: Failures and cleanup are implicit; operational messages or instructions are misleading.
anchors.2: Expected failures/cleanup mostly clear, but important paths need investigation.
anchors.3: Validation, exceptions, cleanup and recovery are explicit; usage is reproducible.
anchors.4: Failure boundaries and recovery are easy to verify; documented commands and test evidence support maintenance.

manual_review.note: A concise easy solution may deserve 4; line count, type hints, docstring count or abstraction count do not mechanically determine quality. Existing scaffold documentation is not credited as new work.

ambiguity_policy: Post-release retry response may be active or released; reservation identity and stock must remain unchanged. Cache thread safety, clock rollback and DAG cancellation/BaseException remain out of scope.
future_protocol: Freeze these files before future inference, use new clean sessions; do not claim historical candidates saw the added rubric or feedback.
reference_correction: Cache reference accepts arbitrary positive integer TTL without float conversion; temporary copy only. Added check uses integer injected clock and TTL=10**400. DAG positive reference accepts a readonly Mapping for added-test portability; no new required Mapping score imposed on candidates.
